## Quarto

Quarto enables you to weave together content and executable code into a finished document. To learn more about Quarto see <https://quarto.org>.

## Running Code

When you click the **Render** button a document will be generated that includes both content and the output of embedded code. You can embed code like this:

```{r}
library(tidyverse)

# 1. Read data
df <- read_csv("results_aggregated.csv",
               col_types = cols())

# 2. Filter by date
target_dates <- c("20251218_200247", "20251219_033312")

df_filtered <- df |>
  filter(date %in% target_dates)

# 3. Aggregate by (mode, rag_k)
df_avg <- df_filtered |>
  group_by(mode, rag_k) |>
  summarise(
    success = mean(success, na.rm = TRUE),
    success_rate = mean(success_rate, na.rm = TRUE),
    rag_k = factor(mean(rag_k)),
    .groups = "drop"
  )
```

You can add options to executable code like this

```{r}
ggplot(df_avg, aes(x = factor(rag_k), y = success_rate, fill = rag_k)) +
  geom_col(
    width = 0.7
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0.3, 0.55)) +
  facet_wrap(~ mode, scales = "fixed") +
  labs(
    title = "Effect of RAG Top-k on Success",
    x = "RAG top-k",
    y = "Success Rate"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 13) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(hjust = .5))
```

The `echo: false` option disables the printing of code (only output is displayed).

```{r}
library(tidyverse)

# 1. Read data
df <- read_csv("results_aggregated.csv",
               col_types = cols())

# 2. Filter target dates
target_dates <- c("20251218_200247", "20251219_033312")

df_filtered <- df |>
  filter(date %in% target_dates)

# 3. Aggregate by (mode, rag_k)
#    Sum error counts across runs
df_err <- df_filtered |>
  group_by(mode, rag_k) |>
  summarise(
    WA = mean(WA, na.rm = TRUE),
    TLE = mean(TLE, na.rm = TRUE),
    COMPLEXITY = mean(COMPLEXITY, na.rm = TRUE),
    RE = mean(RE, na.rm = TRUE),
    exception = mean(exception, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

# 4. Pivot to long format
df_err_long <- df_err |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(WA, TLE, COMPLEXITY, RE, exception),
    names_to = "error_type",
    values_to = "count"
  )

# 5. Bar plot with facet by (mode, rag_k)
ggplot(df_err_long, aes(x = error_type, y = count)) +
  geom_col(
    fill = "grey60",
    width = 0.7
  ) +
  facet_grid(
    rows = vars(mode),
    cols = vars(rag_k),
    scales = "fixed"
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Error Type Distribution by Mode and RAG Top-k",
    x = "Error Type",
    y = "Error Count"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 30, hjust = 1),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank()
  )
```

```{r}
#| fig-height: 6.99
#| fig-width: 10

library(tidyverse)

df_plot <- df_err_long |>
  mutate(mode_rag = paste0(mode, "_rag", rag_k))

# 1. Calculate the global error counts wrt mode_rag
mode_rag_totals <- df_plot |>
  group_by(mode_rag) |>
  summarise(total_count = sum(count)) |>
  arrange(desc(total_count)) |>
  slice_head(n = 6)  # First 6

top_mode_rag <- mode_rag_totals$mode_rag

# 2. Filter and keep the first 6 mode_rag
df_filtered <- df_plot |>
  filter(mode_rag %in% top_mode_rag)

# 3. Set factor levels for mode_rag
df_filtered <- df_filtered |>
  mutate(mode_rag = factor(mode_rag, levels = top_mode_rag))

# 4. Plot
ggplot(df_filtered, aes(x = mode_rag, y = count, fill = mode)) +
  geom_col(width = 0.7) +
  facet_wrap(~ error_type, scales = "free_y", ncol = 3) +
  labs(
    title = "Error Count per Error Type",
    x = "(Mode, RAG top-k)",
    y = "Error Count"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 60, hjust = .9),
    panel.grid.major.x = element_blank(),
    plot.title = element_text(hjust = .5, size = 24))

```
